versions.question: An ALB should pin each client to one target for a fixed period using a cookie the load balancer itself creates. Which stickiness type is this?
options: Duration-based stickiness, where the ALB issues the cookie (named AWSALB)
Application-based stickiness, where the load balancer reads a cookie your targets create
Connection draining set on the target group
Source-IP hashing configured on the listener rule
versions.explanation: Duration-based stickiness uses a cookie generated by the load balancer; application-based stickiness relies on a cookie your target sets.

versions.question: What is the allowed range for the stickiness duration on an ALB target group?
options: From 1 minute to 24 hours, set in whole minutes
From 5 minutes to 30 days, only with custom cookies
A value between 1 second and 7 days, set per target group
From 1 second to 1 year, matching CloudFront's TTL ceiling
versions.explanation: ALB stickiness duration can be set between 1 second and 7 days.

versions.question: Object access in a data lake varies wildly and nobody can predict which files get read. The team wants objects to shift between access tiers on their own with no per-GB retrieval charge. What should they pick?
options: A single-AZ infrequent class that keeps one copy of the data in just one zone
The class that tracks per-object access and moves data between tiers for a small monitoring fee
The class with a 30-day minimum duration and a retrieval fee for every GB read back
The cheapest archival class, whose restores can take up to 12 hours to complete
versions.explanation: Intelligent-Tiering moves objects between tiers based on access, with no retrieval fees.

versions.question: In S3 Intelligent-Tiering, after how many days without access does an object move to the Archive Instant Access tier?
versions.explanation: Objects go Frequent, then Infrequent after 30 days, then Archive Instant Access after 90 days without access.

versions.question: What is the purpose of adding random jitter to an exponential backoff schedule?
options: It lets the client skip retries entirely on throttling errors
It spreads retries so many clients do not hit the service together
It guarantees that each retry succeeds on the very next attempt
It turns the doubling wait into a linear one, which saves total waiting time
versions.explanation: Jitter randomises the waits so clients do not retry in lockstep, reducing pressure on the service.

versions.question: A client waits 3 s, then 6 s, then 12 s between retries after failures. Which retry strategy is this?
options: Fixed-interval polling that always waits the same amount
Linear backoff that adds a constant number of seconds
Exponential backoff, since the delay doubles each time
Immediate retry until a maximum attempt cap is reached
versions.explanation: Each wait is double the previous one, which is exponential backoff.

versions.question: Audit logs must be retained for a decade. They are read perhaps once a year and a 12-hour restore wait is fine. Which S3 class has the lowest storage price?
versions.explanation: Deep Archive is the cheapest S3 storage class and suits long-term, rarely accessed data.

versions.question: Which statement best ranks S3 storage prices per GB?
options: S3 Standard is cheapest because it never charges any retrieval fee at all
Standard-IA is cheapest because there is no retrieval delay or minimum duration
Glacier Deep Archive costs the least of any S3 class per GB stored
One Zone-IA is cheapest because it keeps only one copy of the data in one AZ
versions.explanation: Deep Archive is the lowest-cost class, in exchange for retrieval times measured in hours.

versions.question: A photo site needs full-size uploads served instantly for 30 days, after which a 12-hour restore wait is acceptable. Generated previews can be rebuilt at any time and are only needed for 30 days. Which setup is best?
options: Store originals in One Zone-IA with no lifecycle rule, and store previews in Standard with no expiration, so they stay available forever
Put everything in Intelligent-Tiering and add no lifecycle rules, so previews are never deleted
Place originals and previews in Glacier Flexible Retrieval from the first day, with a lifecycle rule that deletes previews at 30 days
Keep originals in Standard and transition them to Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days; store previews in One Zone-IA and expire them at 30 days
versions.explanation: Originals need hot access first then cheap archival; previews are reproducible so single-AZ storage plus expiry is fine.

versions.question: Scanned receipts need instant access for 90 days, then can be restored within several hours. Thumbnails are re-creatable and only needed for 90 days. Which design fits?
options: Both in Intelligent-Tiering with no lifecycle configuration, so thumbnails stay indefinitely too
Receipts in One Zone-IA forever with no rules; thumbnails moved to an archive tier after a month
Receipts in Glacier Deep Archive from day one; thumbnails in Standard with no expiry date at all
Move receipts from Standard into a hours-restore Glacier tier at 90 days; keep thumbnails in single-AZ infrequent storage with an expiry at 90 days
versions.explanation: Hot-then-archive lifecycle for the irreplaceable data; cheap single-AZ plus expiration for regenerable data.

versions.question: An ASG running a web tier should hold the ALB request count per target near 1,000 with minimal configuration effort. Which scaling approach should be used?
options: Target tracking on ALB request count per target
Scheduled actions that change capacity at fixed clock times each day
Manual changes to the desired capacity whenever traffic looks busy
Simple scaling with a hand-built alarm and a cooldown that must be tuned
versions.explanation: Target tracking keeps a metric near a target value and manages the CloudWatch alarms for you.

versions.question: Which ASG policy type lets you simply state a desired metric value and creates and manages the CloudWatch alarms itself?
options: A target-value policy where the ASG manages the alarms
A manual edit of desired capacity in the console during incidents
Calendar-based actions that set min, max and desired at set times
Step policies with explicit alarm thresholds and step adjustments you define
versions.explanation: Target tracking is the simplest dynamic policy: you choose a target and AWS handles the alarms.

versions.question: Which three items are specified in an EC2 Auto Scaling launch template? (Choose three)
options: The instance profile (IAM role) for the instances
The minimum and maximum size of the group
Block device mappings for the EBS volumes
versions.explanation: A launch template describes how to launch an instance; size limits, policies and grace periods belong to the ASG.

versions.question: Which two settings are NOT part of a launch template but are configured on the Auto Scaling group itself? (Choose two)
versions.explanation: Launch templates define instance config; capacity and scaling policies belong to the ASG.

versions.question: On a laptop, where does the AWS CLI keep access keys, versus the Region and output-format defaults?
options: Keys in `~/.aws/config`; Region only in an environment variable
Both in a single `~/.aws/profile.json` file that the console creates for each user
Keys in `~/.aws/credentials`; Region and output in `~/.aws/config`
Keys in `/etc/aws/keys`; Region in the instance metadata service
versions.explanation: Credentials and config are separate files, each with sections per profile.

versions.question: A developer wants a whole shell session to use a second account's credentials without editing the default settings. What is the easiest way?
options: Delete the default profile and recreate it whenever the account changes
Edit the CLI source so it reads a different home directory
Add the second account's keys to the instance metadata service of the laptop
Export the `AWS_PROFILE` environment variable with the name of the profile
versions.explanation: AWS_PROFILE selects a named profile for every command in the session.

versions.question: Large downloads from S3 by instances in private subnets show up as heavy NAT Gateway data-processing charges. What is the most direct cost fix?
options: Replace the NAT Gateway with a NAT instance of the same size in one AZ
Attach public IPs to the instances and place them in a public subnet
Turn on VPC Flow Logs and analyse the traffic more carefully
Create a gateway VPC endpoint for S3 and route S3 traffic through it
versions.explanation: Gateway endpoints for S3 have no hourly or data-processing charge and bypass the NAT.

versions.question: Which VPC endpoint type for S3 is added as a route table target and carries no additional charge?
options: Gateway Load Balancer endpoint, used for inspection appliances
A gateway endpoint, which is free and added to route tables
Egress-only internet gateway, which handles outbound IPv6 traffic
Interface endpoint, which places an ENI in each subnet and bills hourly
versions.explanation: S3 and DynamoDB gateway endpoints are free and work through route table entries.

versions.question: Which S3 class stores backups that are restored in minutes to hours and offers free bulk retrievals?
versions.explanation: Flexible Retrieval (formerly S3 Glacier) has expedited, standard and free bulk retrievals.

versions.question: Which statement about S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval is correct?
options: Bulk retrievals are free and complete within hours
Reads return in milliseconds like Standard-IA
Data is stored in one AZ only, like One Zone-IA
Every retrieval is billed as an expedited request
versions.explanation: Flexible Retrieval (formerly S3 Glacier) has expedited, standard and free bulk retrievals.

versions.question: A security group must allow administrators to open a remote desktop session to a Windows instance. Which inbound port is needed?
versions.explanation: RDP uses port 3389; SSH on 22 is for Linux.

versions.question: Which protocol is carried over TCP port 3389?
options: Server Message Block, for file shares
versions.explanation: Port 3389 is RDP, used for Windows remote sessions.

versions.question: Which two facts about a VPC peering connection hold true? (Choose two)
options: Peered VPCs talk to each other over private IP addresses
Peering A to B and B to C lets A reach C automatically
Traffic between the VPCs goes out through an internet gateway
A peering connection can link VPCs that live in different Regions
versions.explanation: Peering is non-transitive and uses the AWS network, not the public internet.

versions.question: For two VPCs to talk over a peering connection, which two conditions must hold? (Choose two)
options: The VPC CIDR blocks must not overlap
A NAT Gateway must be placed in a shared subnet
Route table entries pointing at the peering connection must exist on both sides
An internet gateway must be attached to each VPC
versions.explanation: Peering needs non-overlapping CIDRs and routes in both route tables.

versions.question: Which two statements describe security groups? (Choose two)
options: A rule can explicitly deny a single IP address
Rules are evaluated in numbered order, lowest first
Return traffic for an allowed request is permitted automatically
A rule can name another security group as its source
versions.explanation: Security groups are stateful, allow-only and can reference other groups.

versions.question: Which VPC firewall is stateful and supports only allow rules?
versions.explanation: Security groups are stateful and allow-only; NACLs are stateless with allow and deny.

versions.question: What is the default cooldown period of an Auto Scaling group?
versions.explanation: The default cooldown is 5 minutes, letting metrics stabilise after a scaling activity.

versions.question: A group scaled out a minute ago and the alarm is still in ALARM state, yet no further instance launches. What is the most likely reason?
options: The AMI was deregistered in the meantime and nothing can launch
An earlier scaling activity's cooldown is still running
The desired capacity has been set below the group's minimum size
The ALB has cross-zone load balancing disabled on its listener
versions.explanation: During cooldown the ASG waits before launching more instances.

versions.question: An EC2 instance with only instance store volumes is stopped and later started. What happens to the data on those volumes?
options: It is kept because the data is replicated to S3 on stop
It is kept as long as the instance has an Elastic IP
It is lost, because the volumes are tied to the physical host
It is kept for 24 hours after the stop and then removed by a background job
versions.explanation: Stop, terminate or host failure wipes instance store data.

versions.question: Which event leaves data on an instance store volume intact?
versions.explanation: A reboot keeps the same host, so the data stays.

versions.question: Which three capabilities does ElastiCache for Redis offer that Memcached nodes do not? (Choose three)
options: Snapshots that can be restored into a new cluster
Promoting a replica to primary when the primary fails
Rich data types such as sorted sets
Scaling out by adding nodes to a pool
versions.explanation: Redis offers replication, HA, backups and rich data structures.

versions.question: A cache must survive a node failure with automatic failover and keep data across restarts. Which engine fits?
options: Memcached with extra nodes added to the pool for more capacity
DAX placed in front of a DynamoDB table to cache item reads
An S3 bucket with Transfer Acceleration enabled for faster access
Redis, using replicas with failover and snapshot persistence
versions.explanation: Memcached has no replication or persistence; Redis does.

versions.question: Administrators need a command-line shell session on a Linux EC2 instance from their laptop. Which port must the security group allow?
options: TCP 80, the port for unencrypted web traffic
TCP 22, from the administrators' IP range
TCP 3389, the port for Windows remote desktop
TCP 53, the port for DNS lookups
versions.explanation: SSH uses port 22.

versions.question: Which service listens on TCP port 22?
versions.explanation: SSH and SFTP use port 22.

versions.question: Which S3 feature routes uploads through CloudFront edge locations to speed up long-distance transfers to a bucket?
versions.explanation: Transfer Acceleration uses the AWS edge network and works with multipart upload.

versions.question: Video creators worldwide upload big files to one bucket in Frankfurt, and uploads from far away are slow. What is the least-effort improvement?
options: Use a larger EC2 instance as an upload proxy in Frankfurt
Put the bucket behind an Application Load Balancer for the uploads
Create buckets in every Region and merge the data nightly with a custom script
Enable Transfer Acceleration and upload through the accelerated endpoint
versions.explanation: Accelerated endpoints send data to the nearest edge location first.

versions.question: A team needs detailed records of every request to a bucket (requester, key, response code), written to another bucket. What do they enable?
versions.explanation: Server access logging captures request details for auditing.

versions.question: Where must the target bucket for S3 server access logs be located?
options: In a separate account, to prevent tampering
In the same Region as the source bucket
In us-east-1, where the logging service runs
In any Region, delivered over the AWS backbone
versions.explanation: The logging target must be in the same Region.

versions.question: An application adds more EC2 instances when load rises and removes them when it falls. What is this called?
options: Horizontal scaling, adding instances as load rises
Cross-Region failover between two active stacks
Rightsizing the instance type once per quarter
Vertical scaling, moving between instance sizes
versions.explanation: Out/in add or remove instances; up/down change instance size.

versions.question: Moving a workload to a larger instance type is best described as which operation?
versions.explanation: Vertical scaling is up/down; horizontal is out/in.

versions.question: In the LAMP stack, which component does the letter **A** stand for?
versions.explanation: LAMP = Linux, Apache, MySQL, PHP.

versions.question: A team hosts a PHP site on Linux EC2 with Apache and a relational database. In the LAMP name, which letter represents the database?
versions.explanation: In LAMP the M is MySQL (MariaDB is a drop-in alternative).

versions.question: A company wants to be sure an EC2 instance type is available in one AZ when needed. Which purchase option guarantees that, and does it lower the hourly price by itself?
options: A Capacity Reservation: capacity is guaranteed, billing stays at the On-Demand rate
A Spot Fleet request guarantees capacity and cuts the price by 70%
A Capacity Reservation guarantees capacity and also provides a discount
A Dedicated Host reservation guarantees capacity and discounts all usage
versions.explanation: Capacity Reservations are about availability, not price.

versions.question: How can you both guarantee capacity in a Region and get a discount?
options: Use Spot Instances placed in a cluster placement group
Use only a Zonal Reserved Instance without any reservation
Use a Capacity Reservation by itself, as that already lowers the hourly rate
Pair a Capacity Reservation with a Savings Plan or Regional Reserved Instance
versions.explanation: The discount comes from a Savings Plan or Regional RI applied to matching usage.

versions.question: Which statement about S3 durability across storage classes is correct?
options: Durability is 100% because objects are replicated across Regions
Durability is highest in S3 Standard only and drops in the infrequent classes
Durability falls to 99.9% in Glacier Deep Archive
Durability is 11 nines in every class; only availability differs
versions.explanation: Durability is the same everywhere; availability varies.

versions.question: What does the 99.999999999% figure for S3 describe?
options: The chance of not losing an object over a year
The probability that a Region stays online
The percentage of time the service responds to requests
The share of requests answered in milliseconds
versions.explanation: That is durability; availability is a separate number by class.

versions.question: Which three items are parts of an S3 object? (Choose three)
options: IAM role attached to the object
Version ID when versioning is enabled
versions.explanation: An object has key, value, metadata, tags and version ID.

versions.question: In S3, what is the name for the full path that identifies an object in a bucket?
versions.explanation: The key is the object's full path name.

versions.question: Which caching strategy is the recommended starting point?
options: Caching every table in full at startup
Disabling expiry so data never goes stale
Write-through for all data from day one
Lazy loading, adding TTLs for freshness
versions.explanation: Lazy loading is simple; add write-through only if staleness is a problem.

versions.question: Which data suits caching best?
options: Records that are read exactly once and never again
Values that change on every single request
Account balances that must be exact at every single read
Data where slight staleness is acceptable to users
versions.explanation: Cache data tolerant of slight staleness.

versions.question: Which two S3 classes give millisecond access across several AZs while charging retrieval per GB? (Choose two)
versions.explanation: IA and Glacier Instant Retrieval are immediate; the other Glacier classes need waiting.

versions.question: Which S3 infrequent-access class stores data in a single AZ only?
versions.explanation: One Zone-IA is single AZ; the others are multi-AZ.

versions.question: A primary RDS instance's AZ fails. What does Multi-AZ do?
options: Reroutes all traffic to a copy in another Region
Restores the latest manual snapshot onto a brand-new instance in another AZ
Adds read replicas automatically in the surviving AZs
Fails over to the synchronous standby and flips the DNS name
versions.explanation: Multi-AZ gives automatic failover to the standby.

versions.question: How does RDS Multi-AZ replicate data to its standby?
versions.explanation: Replication to the standby is synchronous.

versions.question: Which encapsulation protocol and port does Gateway Load Balancer use to send traffic to appliances?
versions.explanation: GWLB uses GENEVE on port 6081.

versions.question: An inline intrusion-detection fleet of third-party appliances must see all traffic transparently. Which load balancer fits?
versions.explanation: GWLB provides a transparent network gateway plus load balancing for appliances.

versions.question: Which two headers can an origin send to influence how long CloudFront caches an object? (Choose two)
versions.explanation: Origins use Cache-Control and Expires; the cache policy sets min, max and default TTL.

versions.question: What range can TTL be set to in a CloudFront cache policy?
versions.explanation: TTLs go from 0 up to 1 year.

versions.question:
What caching strategy does this code use?

```python
def get_user(uid):
    u = redis.get(f"user:{uid}")
    if u is None:
        u = db.load_user(uid)
        redis.setex(f"user:{uid}", 300, u)
    return u
```
versions.explanation: It populates the cache only on a miss, which is lazy loading.

versions.question: Which strategy loads data into the cache only when a requested item is not found there?
versions.explanation: Lazy loading fills the cache on a miss.

versions.question: Public users must reach an EC2 web server over TLS. Which inbound rule is required?
options: RDP, TCP 3389, source 0.0.0.0/0 for the visitors
SSH, TCP 22, source 0.0.0.0/0 for the visitors
FTP, TCP 21, source 0.0.0.0/0 for the visitors
versions.explanation: HTTPS is port 443.

versions.question: Which TCP port does an HTTPS listener use by default?
versions.explanation: HTTPS uses port 443.

versions.question: A Python Lambda function must write items to DynamoDB. Which tool does it use?
options: An AWS SDK such as boto3
The AWS CLI run by hand
versions.explanation: Application code uses SDKs.

versions.question: The AWS CLI is built on top of which SDK?
versions.explanation: The CLI is built on the Python SDK.

versions.question: A game ranks players by score in real time. Which Redis structure suits this?
versions.explanation: Sorted sets order members by score.

versions.question: Which data type keeps members ordered by a numeric score, making top-N queries cheap?
versions.explanation: Sorted sets are used for leaderboards.

versions.question: Visitors get 403 Forbidden from an S3 website. What fixes it?
options: Turn on cross-region replication from a second bucket in another Region
Enable Requester Pays so visitors cover the cost
Add a lifecycle rule moving pages to Standard-IA
Disable Block Public Access and add a bucket policy allowing s3:GetObject
versions.explanation: Website content needs public read access.

versions.question: Which bucket policy statement lets anonymous visitors read website objects?
options: Deny, Principal *, Action s3:PutObject on the bucket's objects
Allow, Principal *, Action s3:GetObject on the objects
Allow, Principal root only, Action s3:ListAllMyBuckets
Allow, Principal *, Action s3:DeleteObject on the bucket
versions.explanation: GetObject for everyone allows public reads.

versions.question: Which EBS volume supports up to 256,000 IOPS?
versions.explanation: io2 Block Express reaches 256,000 IOPS.

versions.question: A database needs 100,000 sustained IOPS with sub-millisecond latency on a Nitro instance. Which volume?
options: st1 with a large volume size for more baseline
gp2 with a very large size to earn burst credits
gp3 with throughput raised to its maximum value
versions.explanation: Only io2 Block Express provides this.

versions.question: What IP requirement exists for creating a VPC peering connection?
options: Both VPCs must share an Availability Zone
Both VPCs must belong to the same account
The CIDR ranges must not overlap
Both VPCs must be in the same Region
versions.explanation: Overlapping CIDRs cannot be peered.

versions.question: Two merged companies both used 172.31.0.0/16 default VPCs. Can they be peered?
options: Yes, if the VPCs are in different Regions
Yes, with a NAT Gateway in each VPC
Yes, AWS translates the addresses automatically
No, the overlapping ranges block peering
versions.explanation: CIDRs must not overlap.

versions.question: Which three reasons justify RDS Proxy? (Choose three)
options: Many Lambda invocations sharing a small connection pool
Using IAM auth with credentials in Secrets Manager
versions.explanation: RDS Proxy pools connections, speeds failover, and enforces IAM auth.

versions.question: Lambda functions exhaust database connections. Which service helps?
versions.explanation: RDS Proxy pools connections.

versions.question: How many tags can a single S3 object carry at most?
versions.explanation: Up to 10 tags.

versions.question: Which two uses do S3 object tags have? (Choose two)
versions.explanation: Tags drive lifecycle and access control.

versions.question: Which feature recommends when to move data from Standard to Standard-IA by observing access?
versions.explanation: Analytics gives transition recommendations.

versions.question: Storage Class Analysis gives recommendations for which transitions?
versions.explanation: Only Standard and Standard-IA.

versions.question: A domain is registered elsewhere and the team wants Route 53 to answer DNS queries. After creating a public hosted zone, what next?
options: Create a private hosted zone and copy its NS values
Create an Alias record at the registrar pointing to the zone
Transfer the domain to Route 53 first, since zones need registered domains
Update the registrar's name servers to the zone's NS values
versions.explanation: Registrar and DNS service are separate.

versions.question: Which hosted zone type answers queries from the public internet?
versions.explanation: Public zones serve internet DNS.

versions.question: Which two failures should a client retry with backoff? (Choose two)
versions.explanation: Retry server and throttling errors.

versions.question: Which error is not worth retrying?
versions.explanation: Fix client errors rather than retrying.

versions.question: A launch script should run at first boot to install packages. Which feature?
versions.explanation: User data bootstraps instances.

versions.question: With which privileges does EC2 user data run by default?
versions.explanation: Runs as root.

versions.question: A scratch cache needs millions of IOPS from locally attached disks. What storage fits?
versions.explanation: Instance store offers the highest local performance.

versions.question: Which storage is physically attached to the host and ephemeral?
versions.explanation: Instance store is ephemeral.

versions.question: Clients need fixed IPs and path-based routing. Which design fits?
options: An NLB forwarding to an ALB
An ALB with static IP addresses assigned directly to the load balancer
A GWLB in front of the app
versions.explanation: NLB gives static IPs, ALB gives Layer 7 routing.

versions.question: Which load balancer provides static IPs per AZ?
versions.explanation: NLB supports Elastic IPs.

versions.question: How are AWS API requests authenticated?
options: Matched by source IP address to a registered IAM principal on file
Signed with SigV4 using the caller's credentials
The User-Agent header the SDK sets
A password passed in the URL
versions.explanation: Requests are signed with SigV4.

versions.question: Where can a SigV4 signature be placed in a request?
options: In the request body only, as a JSON field
In a cookie only, set after a console login
In the Authorization header or the query string
In the TLS client certificate presented
versions.explanation: Header or query string.

versions.question: What can S3 static website hosting serve?
options: PHP pages executed on the bucket
Node.js apps running on the bucket
Python apps running on the bucket
versions.explanation: Static only.

versions.question: What does S3 website hosting need server-side?
options: A container cluster behind the bucket
No servers to manage at all
An EC2 instance running a web server
A Lambda function for each page
versions.explanation: It is serverless.

versions.question: An RDS database is overloaded by repetitive reads. Best fix?
options: Enable Multi-AZ on the DB instance to add a standby in another AZ
Put ElastiCache in front for repeated reads
Grow the volume with automatic scaling
Lengthen the backup window each night
versions.explanation: Caching removes repeat queries.

versions.question: What must you change to use ElastiCache?
versions.explanation: Needs code changes.

versions.question: A clustered app needs a shared block volume across instances in one AZ. Which?
versions.explanation: Multi-Attach.

versions.question: Which volume types support EBS Multi-Attach?
versions.explanation: io1/io2 only.
